While he's not gone on Tapeta since his first three career runs it's worth noting he was runner-up in two of those and probably represent two of his best efforts. Billy Bathgate is a danger to all but is unreliable and Ebony Maw has a bit to prove off a layoff having lost form at the end of last season

The host of others with a chance are headed by the unexposed Savvy Kingdom who ran a blinder when placed on first try as far as a mile off an 18-month absence and if able to build on that will go close

The maiden tag could go. Benacre has to be excused a below par effort last time but should be more comfortable back in this grade and rates a big threat but Project Geoffin is feared most. The form of Geoff Oldroyd's gelding dipped late last term but he won a class 5 handicap over course and distance in October and followed it up with a fine second upped to this level. Off the same mark and with a good record fresh (4th of 19 last year and second on career debut in 2023) he shouldn't be far away

selections.comment: Pop Favorite had almost two lengths to spare over Cuban Fiesta when winning over course and distance a few weeks back. With Cuban Fiesta getting a 4lb pull it's likely to be very tight this time  and both can play a big role again but MADAME PLAINTIFF is taken to make a starring role on her stable debut having moved from Ireland. She was placed off this mark on her penultimate start seeing out the mile powerfully and should find this company a shade more accomadating than she's got accustomed to. A winner first tme out last year there's every chance of a big run if taking to this new surface

selections.comment: SPARTAN FIGHTER looks the value call in a tight race. The veteran's last run is best ignored as he palpably did not get the trip on his first try over a mile in an 82 race career. He went well here over 7f prior to that but is best at this 6f. He can gain a seventh course and distance win off a career low mark. The most obvious danger is Asadjumeirah who has been in solid form this year with two wins and three seconds already. Over his optimum conditions he should go close again. Another showing remarkable resilience is May Remain who desperately deserves reward for some cracking efforts in a very busy year so far despite often not enjoying the rub of the green. If Ivan Furtado's gelding is 1lb well in for future races and if not feeling the effects of a third run in a week the warrior can get a podium finish

selections.comment: A field of unexposed potentially classy types headed by the unbeaten ALPINE TRAIL who is expected to take this step up in grade in his stride. He overcame greenness to win on debut in the winter before following up on turf last month beating a next time out winner decisively. That proved his stamina for 10f and he can make his fitness edge over his main rival Aurel tell. That rival impressed when making a winning debut over the winter despite being given plenty to do and the form of that race has worked out extremely well. His yard is in good form though their horses have tended to come on for their reappearances. The form of Ernst Blofeld's debut effort took a boost over the weekend and he justified strong support easily next time. He could complete the tricast.

selections.comment: The unbeaten COSMIC YEAR looks set to continue his progression up in class. He couldn't have been more impressive on the AW last time and there was plenty of Guineas talk after the race. That doesn't seem unfounded given he had plenty left in the tank in both his wins and this easier task should be no problem. Symbol Of Honour finished behind The Waco Kid and Diego Ventura here in the Tattersalls Stakes last autumn but he has progressed significantly in Dubai over the winter and should be up to reversing that form. The horse he beat in the first of those Meydan victories has won twice at Group level over there since so he should be capable in this grade. Pellitory had a busy 2yo campaign and has continued his progression at 3 winning over C&D on his return. He will be ridden to pick up the pieces and could stay on into a place.

selections.comment: Charlie Appleby has started the season in good form and he holds a strong hand here at his local track with SPECTACTULAR VIEW and Wild Nature. The former was successful on the AW over the winter and that race has thrown up multiple winners since so he isn't dismissed on his return. However, he is stable second string on jockey bookings and is more exposed than his stablemate who is open to plenty of improvement on his handicap debut. He showed a willing attitude when runner up last time and the third has won since suggesting that this opening mark of 88 may underestimate him. Dante's Lad beat the less fancied of the Appleby pair last time and faces that rival on better terms. He should be thereabouts if building on that stable debut off what looks a generous opening mark based on his 2yo Irish form which has been franked multiple times at Group level.

selections.comment: MISS INFORMATION travelled strongly here last time before ultimately finding little for pressure looking in need of the run. She perfromed well off similar marks in top handicaps last summer and with that run under her belt is expected to resume her progress. Fifty Nifty was ahead of her that day and looked an unlucky loser after being forced to wait for a run. He is also entitled to come on for that run and rates a big threat though out of form veteran Jumby is weighted to possibly reverse form with that rival after a summer defeat of around 1l here. Physique was too keen here last time but is on the same mark off which he won at Galway last summer and he shaped with plenty of promise against a draw bias on stable debut in the spring. He may prove the biggest danger.

selections.comment: A tight contest where none of the quartet can really be ruled out but SILVER KNOTT appeals most. He took the City Of Gold Stakes in Dubai last time adding to his trio of Graded successes in the US last summer. That form was matched last year by Ambiente Friendly who travelled strong when placing the Derby at Epsom and in Ireland. However, his form tailed off last year and he was disapponting both in his appearance and in the race on his return. After that flat effort, he is probably best watched. Bellum Justum is probably the pick of the Balding pair with Oisin Murphy jocked up and he would hold every chance if back to the level of form which saw him place in a strong Hampton Court last summer.

selections.comment: An open finale which can go to ORNOLULU who never got a gap on the AW last time and finished full of running. He's never won off a mark this year but has proven competitive off this rating of late and he should get a decent pace to aim at here. He was disappointing when last seen on the turf last summer but he has won on fast ground before and proved himself equally effective on the grass in 2023. The consistent Circe has proven himself versatile over a variety of trips on differing ground and remains unexposed over sprint distances. He can chase the selection home ahead of Santa Savana who was highly tried at 2 and should come on for her latest outing.
